note: mapping_basis=data_labels. DERIVATION is core model s3 pattern 1: data/spain_2014_family.do infixes DA3032 at the ES3032 DATA LIST positions (P201..P210 = cols 38-47, identical to ES3032 lines 3-4 and to the questionnaire's column codes (38)-(47)) under lower-cased names, and Bookmark 2 sets item = the variable name (p201..p210; lower-casing is Stata naming) -- nothing positional, so Step 5b is exempt and no verification_/verify_ files were written. LABELS vs QUESTIONNAIRE: ES3032 VARIABLE LABELS P201-P210 were compared with the P.2 rows of cues3032.pdf read from a 300-dpi render of scanned page 1 (not OCR), dot leaders dropped and the two hyphenated line breaks rejoined ('dis-/pone', 'forma-/ción'): 10/10 agree character for character (asserted in build.R), so item_text is both the label and the questionnaire row, with no override. VALUE LABELS identical on all 10: 1 'Muy satisfecho/a' 2 'Bastante satisfecho/a' 3 'Poco satisfecho/a' 4 'Nada satisfecho/a' 7 'N.P.' 9 'N.C.'; option_text uses these full labels (the questionnaire's column headers abbreviate them to 'Muy satisf.' etc.). No N.S. (8) code exists for P.2. RESP BY DESIGN: the .do recodes 7 (N.P., no procede) and 9 (N.C.) to missing, so live resp is {1,2,3,4}; 1 = most satisfied. N.P. is printed on the questionnaire only for the rows for which the question can be inapplicable -- work, household income, salary, partner -- and DA3032 carries code 7 only on those four: p201 1190, p202 55, p207 872, p210 560 (so p201 n=1262 and p207 n=1575 are about half the sample by design: no job / no salary). Code 9 dropped per item p201..p210: 12/25/16/7/11/27/17/21/6/9. DA3032 carries no blanks, 0, 5, 6 or 8 in cols 38-47; 3 respondents (rows 15, 1024, 1345) gave 9 on all ten items and have no rows, which is why live has 2461 of 2464 ids. CHECKED, decisive: reading DA3032 (2464 records, all 385 bytes; id = row number) at cols 38-47, dropping 7/9 as the .do does, with cov_sex col 254 and cov_age cols 255-256 (99 -> NA), reproduces the live table exactly: 21812 rows both, 2461 ids both, 0 only-live / 0 only-rebuilt rows, 0 resp, 0 cov_sex and 0 cov_age mismatches; cov_sex stored as the Stata value label (Hombre 10853 rows, Mujer 10959). Live item x resp (1/2/3/4): p201 383/637/181/61, p202 135/1005/1003/241, p203 459/1252/647/90, p204 653/1555/206/43, p205 629/1357/421/46, p206 469/1588/338/42, p207 94/612/689/180, p208 417/1297/647/82, p209 1354/1014/77/13, p210 1111/716/44/24 -- every item uses all four levels. Coherence: family (mean 1.5) and partner (1.5) most satisfying, household income (2.6) and salary (2.6) least, as expected in 2014 Spain. validate_items.R --table-sets passed (10 items, resp {1,2,3,4}). TEXT (text_source=study_materials): instructions = the full P.2 question text verbatim from cues3032.pdf, shared by all ten rows, so instructions not section_prompt, one trivial section. translation_source=machine_translation: CIS publishes Estudio 3032 in Spanish only; the _translated columns are English written by this project (Bastante/Poco -> Quite/Slightly, as in the sibling tables; the gendered 'satisfecho/a' collapses to 'satisfied') -- issues-page line owed at upload. RIGHTS: instrument_rights_register.csv CIS row (verdict allow, 2026-09-22, widened to every CIS survey year 2026-09-23, irw#2381) applied, not re-derived. public_note: Not-applicable answers (no job, no income, no salary, no partner; asked only for work, household income, salary and partner) were recoded to missing along with no-answer, so those four items have smaller n by design; item text English is IRW machine translation of the Spanish-only CIS questionnaire
